findings.title: Missing Input Validation for Percentage
findings.description: The `calculateDiscount` function does not implement the critical requirement to throw a `RangeError` if the `percentage` is less than 0 or greater than 100. This can lead to incorrect calculations (e.g., negative prices or prices increasing instead of decreasing) and violates the user's objective.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an `if` statement at the beginning of the `calculateDiscount` function to check if `percentage < 0` or `percentage > 100`. If either condition is true, throw a `RangeError` with an appropriate message.

findings.title: Incomplete Unit Test Coverage
findings.description: The unit tests do not cover the critical requirement for input validation. There are no tests to ensure that `calculateDiscount` throws a `RangeError` when `percentage` is outside the valid range (i.e., less than 0 or greater than 100). The automated verification results only show one passing test for a 'standard discount'.
findings.suggestedFix: Add new test cases to `test/discount.test.js` that specifically assert that `calculateDiscount` throws a `RangeError` when `percentage` is, for example, -1, 101, or any other value outside the [0, 100] range. Use `assert.throws` for this purpose.

capturedReviews.summary: The `calculateDiscount` function is missing critical input validation for the `percentage` parameter, which is a direct violation of the user's objective. Consequently, the unit tests are also incomplete as they do not cover this required validation. This could lead to incorrect behavior and unexpected results if invalid percentages are passed to the function.

The implementation correctly calculates discounts and includes robust input validation as required. All specified edge cases, including `RangeError` for out-of-bounds percentages and negative prices, and `TypeError` for non-numeric inputs, are handled. The provided tests cover these scenarios adequately. The code adheres to the user's objective and repository instructions.
